autonomyRules.description: A new lead or commentary link is published automatically and marked unverified.
Confirming a record against an official or regulator source, with nothing else changed, updates its last-verified date automatically.
A new Anticipated record from a rank 1 or 2 source waits for review.
Any other new record sets a status, a date and a tier, so it waits for a named approver.
A status change, effective date or tier change waits for review; the approver is named on the record.
Removal or supersession waits for review; the superseded version is kept.
Any other change to a published record waits for review.

languageRules.description: Records describe what a source says; they never tell a reader what to do.
No record, screen, export or response states whether anyone is compliant or in breach.
'Required' is reserved for counsel's determination; records use source-describing words instead.
Nothing states what the law requires of a particular client; counsel decides what applies.
An Anticipated record shows its trigger date or status, never a likelihood that it will pass or apply.

record.title: ASIC: urgent cyber uplift as AI accelerates cyber threats
record.statement: ASIC's 8 May 2026 release and open letter describe cyber resilience as 'a core licensing obligation, not simply an IT issue', note that frontier AI models are accelerating vulnerability discovery and exploitation, and set out 12 recommended steps (including prompt patching, limiting user access, incident response preparation and third-party risk management). The release states that entities are to table the letter at their ultimate board and risk governance committees.

source.instrument: ASIC open letter to AFS licensees and market participants on cyber resilience (media release 26-092MR)

effectiveDates.note: Media release 26-092MR

record.title: Market participant controls over algorithmic, AI and ML trading systems
record.statement: ASIC's 24 September 2026 release states the amended rules modernise trading systems obligations to cover 'algorithmic trading, AI and machine learning', require participants to have controls to 'test, monitor and govern trading systems and algorithms', and clarify that the false or misleading appearance rule covers AI-enabled trading activity. The changes take effect in 2028 after an 18-month transition.

source.instrument: ASIC Market Integrity Rules (Securities Markets) 2017 and (Futures Markets) 2017, as amended by Amendment Instruments 2026/574 and 2026/575

record.title: ASIC on licensee AI governance and existing obligations
record.statement: REP 798 reviews AI use by 23 AFS and credit licensees and states the regulatory framework is technology neutral. It identifies existing obligations engaged by AI use: providing services efficiently, honestly and fairly; avoiding unconscionable conduct and false or misleading representations about AI; adequate technological and human resources; adequate risk management systems; remaining responsible for outsourced functions to third-party AI providers; and directors' duties of care and diligence. It poses 11 questions, including whether an AI inventory is maintained and what human oversight is expected.

source.instrument: ASIC Report 798 Beware the gap: Governance arrangements in the face of AI innovation
source.citation: REP 798, pp 34-36 (existing obligations; questions for licensees); Findings 1-8

effectiveDates.note: Page states 'Released 29 October 2024' (metadata shows 28 Oct)

record.title: ASX guidance on confidentiality, leaks and monitoring
record.statement: GN 8 explains that a sudden unexplained price or volume movement 'could indicate that the information has leaked' and may be evidence the information is no longer confidential (s 4.2), that entities should have appropriate reporting, escalation and compliance systems (ss 4.4-4.5), and that entities should monitor for leaks while announcements are pending (s 4.6). Section 5.8 addresses the requirement in LR 3.1A.2 for information to be confidential.

source.instrument: ASX Listing Rules Guidance Note 8 Continuous Disclosure: Listing Rules 3.1-3.1B

tierBasis.note: Rests on ASX Listing Rule 3.1A.2

record.title: Continuous disclosure carve-out depends on confidentiality
record.statement: Listing Rule 3.1 requires immediate disclosure of market-sensitive information; Listing Rule 3.1A excepts information only while each condition is met, including 3.1A.2: 'The information is confidential and ASX has not formed the view that the information has ceased to be confidential'. If confidentiality is lost (e.g. through a leak), the carve-out ceases to apply and Listing Rule 3.1 again calls for immediate disclosure.

source.authority: ASX Limited (ASX Compliance); listing rules enforceable under Corporations Act s 793C and linked to s 674

record.title: Board ultimately responsible for risk management framework and risk appetite
record.statement: CPS 220 para 9 provides that the Board of an APRA-regulated institution is ultimately responsible for the institution's risk management framework, including that 'it sets the risk appetite within which it expects management to operate'.

record.statement: CPS 230 para 35 defines critical operations; para 36 lists operations that must at a minimum be classified as critical (e.g. payments, claims processing); para 38 requires tolerance levels for each critical operation; para 40 sets minimum BCP contents; and para 42 requires notification to APRA as soon as possible and not later than 24 hours after a disruption to a critical operation outside tolerance.

record.statement: CPS 234 para 13 provides that the Board is ultimately responsible for the information security of the entity; para 15 requires an information security capability commensurate with the size and extent of threats to its information assets; para 18 requires an information security policy framework.

record.title: Six essential practices for responsible AI adoption
record.statement: The Guidance sets out six essential practices: (1) Decide who is accountable; (2) Understand impacts and plan accordingly; (3) Measure and manage risks; (4) Share essential information; (5) Test and monitor; (6) Maintain human control. It is described as the first update to the Voluntary AI Safety Standard, condensing its 10 guardrails into 6 practices, and the National AI Plan describes its measures as voluntary.

source.authority: National Artificial Intelligence Centre (Department of Industry, Science and Resources)
source.instrument: Guidance for AI Adoption (Foundations and Implementation Practices)

effectiveDates.note: Released by the National AI Centre

record.title: Mandatory AI guardrails proposal - not proceeding
record.statement: The proposals paper consulted on mandatory guardrails for AI in high-risk settings. The consultation page states the Government 'will not proceed at this time with previous proposals' and that feedback informed the National AI Plan, which relies on existing largely technology-neutral laws, with targeted laws 'where needed', and an AI Safety Institute to advise regulators.

source.authority: Department of Industry, Science and Resources
source.instrument: Introducing mandatory guardrails for AI in high-risk settings: proposals paper

record.statement: The Voluntary AI Safety Standard set out 10 voluntary guardrails for AI. The Guidance for AI Adoption (October 2025) describes itself as the first update to the Standard and streamlines the 10 guardrails into 6 practices.

record.statement: Section 20 sets out the accountability obligations of an accountable entity, including to take reasonable steps to conduct its business with honesty and integrity and with due skill, care and diligence. record.title: Accountability obligations of accountable persons
record.statement: Section 21 sets out the accountability obligations of an accountable person, including to act with honesty and integrity and with due skill, care and diligence, to deal with the Regulators in an open, constructive and cooperative way, and to take reasonable steps to prevent matters that would adversely affect the entity's prudential standing or reputation (s 21(d) also covers material contraventions of specified laws). Section 10 defines an accountable person by reference to senior executive responsibility for management or control of the entity or a significant or substantial part of its operations.

record.title: OAIC guidance on ADM privacy policy transparency
record.statement: On 30 September 2026 the OAIC published an APP 1.7-1.9 Transparency Obligation fact sheet, a supplementary fact sheet for government agencies, a flowchart, and an update to Chapter 1 of the APP Guidelines explaining how entities that arrange for computer programs to make or inform significant decisions should describe this in their privacy policies from 10 December 2026.

source.instrument: OAIC APP Guidelines Chapter 1 (APP 1) update and APP 1.7-1.9 Transparency Obligation Fact Sheet and Flowchart
source.citation: APP Guidelines Chapter 1; Fact Sheet; Flowchart

tierBasis.note: Rests on Privacy Act 1988 Sch 1 APP 1.7-1.9

effectiveDates.note: OAIC media release

record.title: Privacy policy disclosure of automated decisions (APP 1.7-1.9)
record.statement: APP 1.7 provides that an APP entity's privacy policy must contain the APP 1.8 information where the entity has arranged for a computer program to make, or do a thing substantially and directly related to making, a decision that could reasonably be expected to significantly affect the rights or interests of an individual, using personal information about the individual. APP 1.8 requires the policy to describe the kinds of personal information used and the kinds of decisions made solely by, or substantially assisted by, such programs; APP 1.9 provides that making a decision includes refusing or failing to make one.

source.instrument: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), Schedule 1 (APPs), as amended by the Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024
source.citation: APP 1.7, 1.8, 1.9 (inserted by POLA Act 2024 Sch 1 Part 15, item 88; application item 89)

record.title: Model AI governance framework for agentic AI
record.statement: The framework recommends measures for organisations deploying AI agents across four dimensions: assessing and bounding risks up front (including limiting agents' autonomy and access to tools and data); keeping humans meaningfully accountable through human-approval checkpoints; technical controls across the agent lifecycle; and enabling end-user responsibility through transparency and training. It is described as 'a living document'.

source.instrument: IMDA Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI

effectiveDates.note: Launched at WEF Davos
Updated version (multi-agent systems, third-party agents, automation bias) per IMDA press release - confirmed only via Allen & Gledhill lead

record.title: Model AI governance framework for generative AI
record.statement: IMDA's Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI, launched 30 May 2024, extends Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework (introduced 2020) to generative AI. It is cross-sector, non-statutory guidance; AI Verify is the associated testing framework and toolkit.

source.instrument: IMDA Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI (and Model AI Governance Framework, 2nd ed.)

effectiveDates.note: Launch per IMDA factsheet dateline

record.title: Board and senior management oversight of AI risk
record.statement: Section 3 provides that the board and senior management should ensure existing risk management frameworks adequately identify, assess and address AI risks (3.2); the board or a delegated committee approves and regularly reviews the overall AI governance approach and ensures AI risks are 'explicitly addressed within the FI's risk appetite framework' (3.4); senior management implements AI risk frameworks and sets up 'an internal escalation process for managing material risks and exceptions from AI use' (3.5); local senior management remains accountable for Singapore-specific considerations (3.6).

source.instrument: MAS Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence Risk Management

effectiveDates.note: Consultation Paper P017-2025 published 13 Nov 2025

Para 1.8: Guidelines take effect
Sections 3 (AI Oversight) and 4 (Key AI Risk Management Systems, Policies and Procedures) may be met from 7 Oct 2027

record.title: AI identification and AI inventory
record.statement: Para 4.2 provides that an FI should establish systems, policies and procedures to ensure consistent identification of AI use across the FI; para 4.5 that it should 'establish and maintain an accurate inventory of AI use cases, systems or models', with policies on update frequency.

source.instrument: MAS Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence Risk Management

record.title: AI risk materiality assessment (impact, complexity, reliance)
record.statement: Para 4.10 provides that an FI should establish a methodology to evaluate the risk materiality of each AI use case; para 4.11 that both inherent and residual risk materiality be considered, with residual risk meeting the FI's risk appetite before deployment; para 4.12 lists minimum dimensions of impact, complexity and reliance (including reliance on third-party AI and degree of human oversight).

record.title: Data management, transparency/explainability and fairness controls
record.statement: Para 5.4 provides for data management controls so data used across the AI life cycle is fit for purpose; para 5.5 for controls ensuring an appropriate level of transparency and explainability for an AI use case; para 5.7 that an FI should define what it considers 'fair' outcomes and have controls to identify and mitigate unfair outcomes.

record.title: Human oversight proportionate to risk materiality
record.statement: Para 5.9 provides that an FI should put in place and regularly review controls to ensure appropriate human oversight over an AI use case, system or model, proportionate to risk materiality, taking into account 'automation bias and decision fatigue'.

record.title: Third-party AI: FI retains primary accountability
record.statement: Para 5.10 provides that onboarding, development and deployment controls for third-party AI should be adequate for the risk; para 5.11 that the decision to use third-party AI is the FI's and it 'retains primary accountability for its use of third-party AI'. MAS's release adds that FIs should consider limiting, suspending or replacing a third-party AI service whose risks fall outside risk appetite.

record.title: Guardrails, testing and secure deployment incl. generative AI and agents
record.statement: Para 1.11 notes AI agents 'could autonomously execute unauthorised or erroneous actions'; para 5.15 provides for controls and guardrails before deployment where risks are identified, with generative AI and AI agents tested for key failure modes; para 5.16 that AI systems be secure and supported by technology-risk controls; para 5.22 for technology and cybersecurity reviews so AI is deployed 'into the production environment in a controlled and secure manner'.

record.title: Personal data in AI recommendation and decision systems
record.statement: The Advisory Guidelines explain how the PDPA applies to AI systems: when the Business Improvement and Research exceptions may support use of personal data in development (Parts III), that consent is generally needed and should be meaningful for deployment with notification proportionate to risk (paras 9.1-9.8), that written policies should describe practices and safeguards for fairness (paras 10.1-10.5), and that service providers of bespoke AI systems act as data intermediaries while organisations 'bear the primary responsibility' (para 11). Para 2.2 states they 'are advisory in nature, are not legally binding'.

record.title: Staff copilot drafts and summarises
record.description: An AI assistant drafts, summarises or searches for staff, who remain the authors of what is sent or decided.
examples: Drafting emails or reports with a general-purpose assistant
Summarising a file of documents for a case officer
exclusions: A copilot whose draft is sent without review is UC3 or UC8

record.title: Score or recommendation shown to a decision-maker
record.description: AI produces a score, ranking or recommendation that a person sees and decides on.
examples: Credit risk score shown to a lending officer
Fraud alert reviewed by an analyst
exclusions: If the score decides the case without a person, UC3

record.title: Automated triage or decline
record.description: AI decides how a case, claim or application is routed, or declines it, without a person deciding each case.
examples: Automatic decline of a credit application
Claims triage that fast-tracks or refers claims

record.title: Automated pricing or straight-through payment
record.description: AI sets a price or executes a payment or transaction straight through.

record.title: Agent acting across steps and tools
record.description: An AI agent plans and carries out a task across several steps, calling tools or other systems.
examples: An agent that gathers documents, checks them and prepares a file
exclusions: An agent that writes to systems of record is UC6

record.title: Agent with write access to systems of record
record.description: An AI agent that can create, change or delete entries in systems of record.
examples: An agent that updates customer records or posts ledger entries

record.title: AI inside a provider or the platform behind it
record.description: AI used by a service provider, or by the platform the provider relies on, in delivering a service to the organization.
examples: A provider's claims platform that uses AI
A cloud platform's AI features inside an outsourced service

record.title: Customer-facing assistant
record.description: An AI assistant that customers or members talk to directly.

record.title: AI-generated code in production systems
record.description: Code written or changed with AI assistance that runs in production systems.
examples: Coding assistant output merged into a core banking service

record.title: AI tools reachable by a deal team
record.description: AI tools that people working on a confidential transaction can reach, through which deal information could be exposed.
examples: A general-purpose assistant used to summarise a data room
